## Background: How electricity bills work

<!-- WRITER: This section does the heavy lifting for the non-expert reader.
     ~1 page. Walk through each concept below. Use Switchbox conventions:
     - "poles and wires" for T&D infrastructure
     - "In other words" restatements after technical points
     - Margin definitions for key terms
     - Footnotes for technical depth (e.g., ICC docket numbers)
-->

<!-- CONCEPT 1: The two-part bill -->

:::{.column-margin}
**Supply** is the cost of the electricity itself — the cost of generating power. **Delivery** is the cost of the "poles and wires" that transport that electricity to your home.
:::

<!-- WRITER: Explain that an electricity bill has two main components:
     supply (generation) and delivery (transmission + distribution).
     Use the "poles and wires" plain-English convention.
     "In other words, you pay for the electricity itself,
      and you pay separately to have it delivered to your home." -->


<!-- CONCEPT 2: What a flat rate means -->

<!-- WRITER: Same price per kWh regardless of when you use electricity.
     Currently the default for most ComEd residential customers.
     Simple, predictable — but it doesn't reflect the fact that
     electricity costs more to generate and deliver at certain times. -->


<!-- CONCEPT 3: What DTOU does -->

:::{.column-margin}
**DTOU** stands for Delivery Time-of-Use. It varies only the delivery charge by time of day. The supply charge stays flat.
:::

<!-- WRITER: Explain DTOU. Only the delivery side of the bill changes.
     Supply stays flat. Describe the time periods.
     Key point: this is a modest change — it only touches one piece of the bill.
     Use the rhetorical question device: "Why does this matter?
     Because delivery is only one component of your bill." -->


<!-- CONCEPT 4: What Rate BEST does -->

:::{.column-margin}
**Rate BEST** is a bundled time-of-use structure filed under ICC Docket P2024-0378. It varies both supply and delivery charges by time of day and season.
:::

<!-- WRITER: Explain Rate BEST. Both supply AND delivery vary.
     Supply charges (BESTECs) are seasonal and time-varying.
     Delivery follows the DTOU structure. Plus a flat transmission adder.
     Four daily periods, seasonal supply differentiation.
     Key point: this reshapes more of the bill, so when you use
     electricity matters much more. -->

[^fn-rate-best]: Rate BEST was proposed in ICC Docket P2024-0378. The structure includes time-varying Basic Electric Service Transmission and Energy Charges (BESTECs), a flat transmission adder, and mandatory DTOU delivery rates.


<!-- CONCEPT 5: Why the distinction matters -->

<!-- WRITER: "The more components of the bill that vary by time of day,
     the more a household's usage pattern — when they use electricity,
     not just how much — determines their bill. In other words, under
     Rate BEST, the timing of your electricity use matters far more
     than under DTOU." -->

## Scope and approach

<!-- WRITER: Short prose paragraph(s) setting up the simulation,
     then bolded key assumptions. Hybrid style per outline. -->

<!-- WRITER: Prose paragraph covering:
     - Data: ComEd smart meter data, ~328K households, full service territory
     - Time period: January 2023 (winter peak) and July 2023 (summer peak)
     - Why these months: seasonal extremes, where TOU impacts diverge most
     - What we measure: percentage change in monthly bills vs. flat rate baseline
     - Why percentage changes: JPV insight — bill size scales with income.
       A $10 change means something very different to a household paying $80/month
       vs. $300/month. Percentages put all households on comparable footing.
     - Geographic granularity: Census block groups, mapped to income data
-->

<!-- WRITER: Bolded key assumptions, bulleted: -->

- We simulate bill impacts **under current consumption patterns** — households do not shift their usage in response to the new rate.

::: {.callout-note}
In reality, time-of-use rates are designed to encourage households to shift electricity use away from peak hours. Our estimates represent the impact _before_ any behavioral response — a conservative baseline for evaluating equity impacts.
:::

- **Rate BEST** is constructed as specified in ICC Docket P2024-0378: time-varying BESTECs, a flat transmission adder, and mandatory DTOU delivery, with four daily periods and seasonal supply differentiation.
- Income is proxied at the **Census block group level** using American Community Survey median household income, not individual household income.
- <!-- WRITER: Add other key assumptions as needed (e.g., revenue neutrality removed per client direction) -->
